info.title: Paiflow API v1
info.description:
Execute a deployed deposit-triggered flow (Pay, Split, condition, swap) and poll its on-chain events from your own backend.

Every `/api/v1/deployments/{id}/…` call requires a Bearer credential: a deployment token (`pfk_…`) bound to one deployment, or a developer token (`pfd_…`) with explicit grants to selected existing deployments still owned by the token owner. GET /api/v1/deployments discovers only that credential's eligible deployments. Developer READ_ONLY permits reads, quotes and funding discovery; READ_OPERATE additionally permits preparation, submission, reconciliation and relayer release. See docs/api/developer-token-permissions.md for the complete matrix. No token grants flow/deployment creation or legacy dev/payroll access.

**Execute deposits are signed by the caller.** `execute` returns an unsigned envelope; you sign it with the `from` key, which stays on your side, and post it to `execute/submit`. A leaked token can prepare and relay a deposit you signed. Webhook and early-release operations use the relayer.

Successful responses are `{ "data": … }`. Errors are `{ "error": { code, message, fields?, details? } }`:

| Code | HTTP status |
| --- | --- |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 |
| `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | 402 |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| `VALIDATION` | 422 |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 |
| `UPSTREAM_RPC` | 502 |

Rate limits are per token and per endpoint (each operation lists its own). Allowances are shared across the selected deployments. A token that has been issued or has worked in the last 30 days is subject to nothing else. Any other token is limited per client address before it is looked up: 6000 lookups per 60 seconds, and, after 300 failed authentications in 600 seconds from the address, 60 per 60 seconds. A token refused in the last minute is refused again without a lookup. Refusal of a live developer credential for a missing grant is never negatively cached, so selection edits take effect immediately. So one caller's bad token does not lock out others on the same network.

No account? `POST /api/v1/demo-token` hands you a short-lived token for a shared demo flow, so every call above can be tried straight away.

The public instance runs on Stellar **testnet**. Guide: `docs/api/README.md`.

get.summary: Read live Schedule state and control eligibility
get.description: Uncached reads of snapshot-selected STREAMER controller/asset instance fields, state and permission getters, and token holding balance. availableStroops is vested unpaid payout entitlement, not token balance or a guarantee of sufficient funding; claimedStroops is cumulative claimed entitlement. unvestedStroops is max(balance minus available, zero); retrievableStroops is that difference only while paused and retrieval-permitted. Retrieval returns funds to the contract-configured controller. Reads occur across RPC calls, not an atomic ledger snapshot; amounts are indicative and simulation/execution are authoritative. Contract-address controllers can be read but cannot use this account-wallet signing protocol. Errors never masquerade as zero balances. Active service required; hosted testnet verification remains pending. Rate limit: 20 requests per 60 seconds per token.

SUCCESS/FAILED require durable ledger finality; EXPIRED requires a closed ledger after maxTime plus covered historical NOT_FOUND proof. Missing/lagging history and RPC errors retain reservations. replacementAllowed=true only for durable SUCCESS/FAILED/proven EXPIRED, and new preparation still checks live eligibility. Active deployment service required; retired token access is not reopened. Rate limit: 20 requests per 60 seconds per token.

get.description: Deployment-scoped display reads of current token contracts from supported on-chain instance storage. Schedule, Webhook, time/oracle conditions, Pay, Split and Swap balances are supported candidates; mutable Pay/Split require Dev mode enabled. Swap reports both input and output tokens. Token contract addresses are asset identity; graph asset labels are not authoritative. Balances are not Schedule payout availability or evidence of payment success. The 10-second process-local single-flight cache preserves original readAt/attemptedAt; a Redis per-deployment refresh lease spans replicas (another replica without cached data answers 429), configured unavailable Redis fails closed for refreshes, and no Redis means process-local coordination; poll no faster than every 10 seconds. Each refresh admits at most four workers and 64 contracts, stops scheduling at 25 seconds, with existing finite HTTP timeouts. Errors use null balances and stale:true; partial totals sum only successful reads, never stand for complete balances. Fresh means all supported/holding targets read successfully within the display window, not a ledger-consistent atomic snapshot. Hosted testnet verification remains pending before participant support is claimed. Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

The envelope must be the one `execute` returned, signed by `from`: anything but a single `deposit` call on this flow's trigger contract is refused with `VALIDATION`, as is a fee-bump envelope.

Idempotent on the envelope hash: submitting the same `signedXdr` again never sends a second transaction, it reports the one already on the network. That is also how to check a `PENDING` result. A transaction that reached the network and failed is a `200` with `status: FAILED` and an `error`, not an HTTP error.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

parameters.description: The preparation response's x-history-request-id. Send it with this prepared envelope and reuse it on retries; a new preparation gets a new ID. Optional analytics correlation only: it does not authorize or deduplicate a payment. Reports verify the account, token, deployment, operation and context before linking requests.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: `false` returns PENDING as soon as the network accepts the transaction. Default `true`: wait up to about 25 seconds for a final status, then return `PENDING` if there is none yet. At most 3 calls per token wait at once; a call over that still sends the transaction and returns `PENDING` straight away, as `wait=false` does. Resubmit the same `signedXdr` to check it.

post.summary: Release a timelock branch's before side now
post.description:
Release a timelock branch's before side now (work delivered), ahead of its deadline.

For a flow like 'pay on delivery, refund the client after the deadline': call this when the work is delivered and the relayer pays the before side. Nothing is signed on your side; the token is the authorisation. Unlike `execute`, this sends a transaction and returns once it is final.

After the deadline the contract refuses the before side and this returns `VALIDATION` (422): the condition then releases to its after side automatically. It also returns `VALIDATION` when the condition holds no funds, or when the deployment has several timelock branches and `nodeId` is missing or unknown. The body may be omitted when there is exactly one branch.

Rate limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds per token.

get.summary: Look up an attributed transaction without resubmitting
get.description: Accepts an authorized pfk_ or pfd_ token. SUCCESS and FAILED are final; REJECTED means submission refusal, not on-chain failure. PENDING requires known acceptance. UNKNOWN means an attributed attempt has no established acceptance or finality; it never authorizes a new payment. Unattributed hashes return 404, including missing outside submissions. Supports execute records, queued webhook audit records, early-release audit records, ingested events and verified direct pipeline invocations in recent RPC envelopes. Outside indirect calls and token transfers alone are unsupported. Stored terminal outcomes and ingested events survive RPC retention; missing historical evidence cannot be reconstructed. Poll after 2 seconds, exponentially back off with jitter to 30 seconds; honor Retry-After on 429. RPC failures return 502, never FAILED. One bounded RPC read per request, at most 60/min per deployment across tokens; production requires shared Redis for that RPC budget. Rate limit: 60 requests per 60 seconds per token across transaction hashes.

get.summary: Poll the deployment's events, oldest first
get.description:
Forward-paginated events the app decoded for this deployment's contracts, ascending by `(ledger, eventId)`. This is the app's record, not a raw chain feed: each event appears once (`eventId` is unique).

**Freshness.** When this deployment's events were last collected from the network more than 10 seconds ago, a call collects them first and waits up to 5 seconds for that before answering from the record. So an event usually appears within 10 to 20 seconds of its ledger closing, whoever submitted the transaction (a wallet paying the contract directly, a scanned SEP-7 QR, a scheduled charge), provided you keep polling. Collection is shared by every caller of the deployment: one at a time, and the next no sooner than 10 seconds after the last one ends, so polling faster than that does not make events arrive sooner. A call that arrives while a collection is already running, or when the network is slow, answers with what is recorded, and the event appears on a later call; a background poller also collects every minute. A confirmed `execute/submit` records its own events before it returns.

A swap is `kind: PAYOUT` with `topic: "swap"` and `data` `{ assetIn, assetOut, amountIn, amountOut }`; amounts are stroops as strings.

To poll: store `nextCursor` and pass it back as `cursor`. While `hasMore` is true, ask again straight away; once it is false, wait and ask again with the same cursor. `nextCursor` is never null once the deployment has events: on an empty page it echoes the cursor you sent. It is null only when there are no events and no cursor was sent.

Rate limit: 120 requests per 60 seconds per token.

post.summary: Get a short-lived token for the public demo deployment
post.description:
Public; no token and no account. Returns a bearer token for one shared swapper deployment on testnet, so you can run the calls above before registering. Takes no body. Available only where the public demo is enabled (the testnet instance); 403 otherwise.

**This deployment is shared.** Anyone else holding a demo token can read the events your deposit produces, including the account you deposited from. The swap proceeds are paid to a Paiflow-owned testnet account, not back to you, so the testnet XLM you deposit is spent. Fund a throwaway account with friendbot and never point this at an account you care about.

For an isolated deployment and a token that does not expire in an hour, register, deploy your own flow and mint a token in the **API access** panel.

Rate limit: 3 requests per 3600 seconds per client IP. Rate limit: 60 requests per 3600 seconds instance-wide.
